comments.revenge: This trade was opened within {window} candles of a loss, with a bigger lot. That's the revenge trading pattern: pause first, then ask whether the setup is really there.
comments.slWidened: You moved your SL further away or removed it while the trade was running. Your original plan already decided when your idea was wrong; moving the SL away adds risk after you're in.
comments.noSl: This trade was opened without an SL, so its downside had no limit short of a stop out. Decide where you're wrong before you get in.
comments.riskAbove: Risk was {risk} of your balance, above the {max}% limit. Cut the lot size until the hit at your SL is at most {max}% of your balance.
comments.reasonContradicts: You went {side} because of {reasons}, but that reason points the other way. Take another look at what you actually saw on the chart.
comments.slTooClose: Your SL was only {sl} pips from entry, closer than the average candle length ({range} pips) over the last {candles} candles. Ordinary movement alone can reach it.
comments.feeling: One of your reasons was {reason}. Being honest about that is good. Before you get in, find one thing on the chart that backs the feeling up.

good.sl: your SL was set from the start and never moved away
good.lead: What went well: {items}. Plans like this are what gets scored, whatever happens next.
good.addTp: One more thing: set a TP at least {min}× your SL distance.
good.lowTarget: One more thing: your target was only {rr}× the risk; Disiplin asks for at least {min}×.

advice.none: Your plans followed the Disiplin rules. A run of losses can still happen with a sound plan; that's part of trading.
advice.slAtEntry: Set your SL before you get in. Without one, a single trade can wipe out the account.
advice.riskWithinLimit: Start from risk: decide your SL first, then pick a lot size that keeps the hit at your SL to {max}% of your balance at most.
advice.rewardRisk: Set your TP at least {min}× your SL distance, so one right trade covers more than one wrong one.
advice.slNotWidened: Leave your SL where it is. Moving it away changes the plan halfway through, right when your head is hot.
advice.notRevenge: After a loss, pause. A bigger lot to win it back is an emotional decision, not a chart decision.
